_meta.indication: XEGLYZE is indicated for the topical treatment of head lice infestation in patients 6 months of age and older.

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, multicenter, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group trial
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects 6 months of age and older with active head lice infestation, enrolled by household with the youngest household member as the index subject
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of index subjects who were lice free at all follow-up visits through Day 14
pivotal_trials.n: Trial 001 index ITT: abametapir N=53, vehicle N=55 (both pivotal trials enrolled 704 subjects total)
pivotal_trials.result: Trial 001 primary endpoint (Day 14): 43/53 (81%) abametapir vs 28/55 (51%) vehicle, p=0.001

nct_ctgov.title: A Study of the Efficacy and Safety of Abametapir Lotion Administered for the Treatment of Head Lice Infestation

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, multicenter, vehicle-controlled trial (identical in design to Ha03-001)
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects 6 months of age and older with head lice infestation
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of index subjects who were lice free at all follow-up visits through Day 14
pivotal_trials.n: Trial 002 index ITT: abametapir N=55, vehicle N=53
pivotal_trials.result: Trial 002 primary endpoint (Day 14): 45/55 (82%) abametapir vs 25/53 (47%) vehicle, p<0.001

nct_ctgov.title: Study of the Efficacy and Safety of Abametapir Lotion Administered for the Treatment of Head Lice Infestation

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=1%) were erythema (4.0%), rash (3.2%), skin burning sensation (2.6%), contact dermatitis (1.7%), vomiting (1.7%), eye irritation (1.2%), pruritus, and hair color changes (1%).
target_moa: Abametapir is a metalloproteinase inhibitor from the class of bipyridinium molecules; it chelates metal cations at the active center of metalloproteinases critical to louse egg development, hatching and survival of the head louse.
modality: Small molecule (5,5'-dimethyl 2,2'-bipyridinyl), a topical metalloproteinase inhibitor

rems.type: DRISK concluded that risk mitigation measures beyond professional labeling are not warranted for Xeglyze for the treatment of head lice infestation.

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee meeting was held; no regulatory issues requiring advisory committee input were identified.

basis.text: The NDA was submitted on September 14, 2015 and granted a standard review.

summary.text: Xeglyze (abametapir), a new molecular entity, received a standard review under a traditional NDA. It was originally submitted September 14, 2015; the Agency issued a Complete Response Letter on August 30, 2016 due to manufacturing facility inspection deficiencies. After resubmission, it was approved July 24, 2020 for topical treatment of head lice infestation in patients 6 months of age and older.

citations.quote: The NDA was submitted on September 14, 2015 and granted a standard review.
On August 30, 2016, the Agency issued a Complete Response Letter because of deficiencies discovered during an inspection of Dr. Reddy's Lab Ltd. CTO Unit VI (FEI 3002949085) manufacturing facility.
